content:
I've been using verso-blueprint for a formalization project and I encountered two issues with GitHub actions in the provided default project template:

  1. On first push the GitHub runner seems to start compiling Mathlib from scratch. As a fix, Claude suggested to add this to .github/workflows/pages.yml so that the build would instead run lake exe cache get:
    with:
      warm_dependency_cache: true
  1. After adding some Mathlib imports, GitHub runner would abruptly terminate the build towards the very end with no explanation. After some investigation it turned out that it run out of RAM (apparently the default free GitHub runner has 16 GB of RAM). The workaround Claude suggested is to change ‎scripts/ci-pages.sh so that it builds just the blueprint but not the whole Lean package. Namely, replacing
lake build CliffordProject

with

lake build CliffordProject.Blueprint

This solved my issue. But if somebody needs others to be able to import their project as a Lean package, then this workaround would not work.

I've had memory issues in CI for several projects (even without verso). I use an action to free some space as first CI step. See for example https://github.com/RemyDegenne/brownian-motion/blob/fa590b1a198cb464357c5b773c7451da941acb43/.github/workflows/blueprint.yml#L28

That is indeed the first thing I tried after Calude's suggestion. However, in my case there turned out to still be plenty of space on the hard drive, and the issue was really due to running out of RAM. After Claude investigated RAM usage during build on my local machine it came to the following conclusion:

The root CliffordProject.lean was forcing Lean to load a 2.6 GB olean into memory a second time for no practical benefit, pushing the peak to 27 GB. Targeting CliffordProject.Blueprint directly cuts it to 16 GB and just fits within the runner's limit.
